title: Sicilian Defence
intro: 1.e4 c5: Black fights for the centre from the side and plays for a win. The most popular answer to 1.e4.

lessons.title: The Open Sicilian and the Najdorf
lessons.summary: Trade a side pawn for a centre pawn, then a6.

steps.text: White opens with 1.e4. The Sicilian answers 1...c5: the pawn controls d4 from the side and keeps the game unbalanced.
White develops with 2.Nf3, getting ready for d4.
Play d6: it guards e5 and prepares ...Nf6.
steps.hint: A one-square pawn move in the centre.
steps.ifWrong: This lesson follows the main line with 2...d6.

feedback.b8c6: 2...Nc6 is a popular Sicilian move too. This lesson follows 2...d6.
feedback.e7e6: 2...e6 is a popular Sicilian move too. This lesson follows 2...d6.

steps.text: Take on d4. You swap your side pawn for White's centre pawn.
steps.ifRight: Now you have two centre pawns against White's one.

steps.text: White takes back with the knight: 4.Nxd4.
Develop with an attack on e4.
steps.hint: Your king's knight can hit e4.
steps.ifWrong: Bring out the knight so it attacks e4.

steps.text: White defends with 5.Nc3. Now you choose your Sicilian.
Play the Najdorf: the quiet a6 keeps White's pieces off b5 and prepares ...e5 or ...b5.
steps.hint: A one-square move with the a-pawn.
steps.ifRight: The Najdorf, a favourite of world champions.

feedback.g7g6: That is the Dragon: also excellent, with the bishop going to g7. This lesson shows the Najdorf.

steps.text: Your plan: use the half-open c-file (a rook on c8 later), challenge the centre with ...e5 or ...e6, and expand with ...b5.

lessons.title: The Sicilian middlegame
lessons.summary: Control the c-file, counter in the centre, and expand with ...b5.

steps.text: With ...e5 in place, Black controls f4 and d4. Now Black develops the light-squared bishop to e6, puts a knight on d7, and expands with ...b5 and ...Rc8.
Develop your light-squared bishop to challenge the d5 and c4 squares.
steps.hint: Put the c8 bishop on e6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 9...Be6 to control d5 and connect your queenside pieces.
steps.ifRight: The bishop eyes c4 and stops White from dominating d5 easily.

steps.text: White shifts the queen to d2, preparing Rfd1 and f3.
Develop your queen's knight without blocking the c-file.
steps.hint: Put the b8 knight on d7 so your rook can use c8.
steps.ifWrong: Play 10...Nbd7: on d7 the knight supports ...b5 and keeps the c-file open for your rook.
steps.ifRight: Notice how the c-file stays clear for ...Rc8.

feedback.b8c6: 10...Nc6 is playable too, yet 10...Nbd7 leaves the c-file open for ...Rc8 and supports ...Nb6-c4.

steps.text: White swings a rook to d1 to pressure d6.
Put a rook on the half-open c-file to target c2.
steps.hint: Slide the a8 rook to c8.
steps.ifWrong: Play 11...Rc8 to put pressure down the c-file.
steps.ifRight: Now ...b5, ...Nb6 and ...Nc4 give Black strong queenside counterplay.

steps.text: White played 12.f3 to guard e4. Start your queenside expansion.
steps.hint: Push the b-pawn two squares to gain space and prepare ...Nb6-c4.
steps.ifWrong: Play 12...b5 (or 12...Nb6 or 12...Qc7) to expand on the queenside.
steps.ifRight: Black has great queenside counterplay along the c-file.
